stories.headline: Gears of War: E-Day Pioneers RAM-Saving SSD Streaming Tech
stories.summary: Tom's Hardware UK reveals how Gears of War: E-Day utilizes advanced storage technology to achieve up to 3.7 GB/s SSD streaming speeds, significantly reducing system RAM usage for visually dense environments.
stories.original_title: We tested the RAM-saving storage tech in Gears of War: E-Day — up to 3.7 GB/s of SSD streaming speed saves several gigabytes of system RAM usage — Today we’re focusing on a less-discussed technology that plays an equally important role in bringing this visually rich, densely detailed world to systems with more limited hardware resources: storage technology designed to reduce RAM usage.
stories.why_it_matters: This tech lets games load huge, detailed worlds instantly without clogging up your computer's memory. It means smoother gameplay and richer visuals for players in the near future.
stories.other_side: Gamers with older computers might not see any benefit because their hardware can't handle these new speed requirements anyway.

stories.headline: US Disrupts North Korean 'FaceStealer' Crypto Theft Campaign
stories.summary: The US government has successfully disrupted a North Korean social engineering campaign named 'FaceStealer', which was responsible for stealing over $400 million in cryptocurrency through sophisticated digital theft methods.
stories.original_title: US disrupts North Korean campaign behind $400 million crypto theft
stories.why_it_matters: Stealing billions from crypto wallets is a major threat to digital money safety. Stopping this group helps protect everyday investors from losing their savings to state-sponsored hackers.
stories.other_side: Some argue that stricter regulations on crypto exchanges are needed to prevent these thefts from happening in the first place.

stories.headline: Stela Boot Program Enables macOS on x86-64 PCs via Apple Silicon Emulation
stories.summary: An open-source boot program called Stela allows users to run Apple Silicon macOS on standard x86-64 PCs by emulating an M2 Mac mini and translating ARM64 instructions, although it currently lacks Wi-Fi and sound support.
stories.original_title: Stela, an open-source boot program, runs Apple Silicon macOS on x86-64 PCs by posing as an M2 Mac mini and translating ARM64 to x86-64
stories.why_it_matters: This tool gives PC users a way to run Apple’s software on non-Apple machines for free. It breaks down the wall between different types of computers.
stories.other_side: The software currently has missing features like sound and Wi-Fi, making it frustrating and impractical for daily use right now.

stories.headline: FAA Ground Stop Lifted After Aging Air Traffic Control Technology Fails
stories.summary: The FAA lifted a nationwide ground stop after flights were halted due to failures in aging air traffic control technology, with officials confirming the disruption was not the result of a cyberattack but rather infrastructure obsolescence.
stories.original_title: FAA Lets Flights Resume After Hours-Long Ground Stop. Mullin Says Disruption Wasn’t A ‘Nefarious Attack.’
stories.why_it_matters: Old air traffic control systems caused massive flight delays across the country. Fixing this aging infrastructure is critical to keeping travel safe and reliable.
stories.other_side: Critics say the government failed to upgrade these systems years ago, proving they were unprepared for such obvious risks.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang Agrees to Testify Before Congress Amid Ouster Controversy
stories.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify under oath before Congress, following reports that he was ousted from the company due to allegations involving an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China.
stories.original_title: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Agrees to Testify Before Congress
stories.why_it_matters: A top tech leader facing serious legal questions shows how corporate scandals can shake public trust. His testimony will reveal if company leadership was compromised.
stories.other_side: Many people doubt the seriousness of the "spying" claims and view the whole situation as a media distraction or political drama.

stories.headline: China Deploys Advanced Technology to Modernize Agriculture Harvest
stories.summary: Technology is reshaping China’s agricultural sector, with over 90 percent of the autumn grain harvest gathered early despite disasters, leveraging tech innovations to ensure full-year output exceeds 700 million tonnes.
stories.why_it_matters: Using robots and smart tools to harvest crops ensures food stays plentiful even during bad weather. This boosts global food security by preventing waste.
stories.other_side: Small farmers who cannot afford expensive high-tech equipment may fall behind and lose their livelihoods to larger corporations.

stories.headline: Windows 10 ESU Quality Updates Face Installation Failures
stories.summary: Users are reporting significant issues with Extended Security Updates (ESU) quality updates failing to install on Windows 10, requiring manual intervention via DISM and sfc scans to resolve software distribution problems.
stories.why_it_matters: Windows 10 users are stuck with broken security patches that leave their computers vulnerable. This highlights the messy reality of supporting old software.
stories.other_side: Microsoft argues that forcing upgrades to newer versions is necessary because maintaining old systems costs too much money.

stories.headline: Why Ethernet Cables May Be Slower Than Wi-Fi Due to Hardware Issues
stories.summary: PCMag explores the counterintuitive phenomenon where ethernet connections perform slower than Wi-Fi, attributing the issue to potential hardware faults, software conflicts, or other underlying technical anomalies in network infrastructure.
stories.original_title: The weird reasons why your ethernet cable might be slower than your Wi-Fi
stories.why_it_matters: Wired internet is often faster than wireless, but faulty cables can ruin that advantage. Knowing this helps users fix slow connections without blaming their internet provider.
stories.other_side: Some experts claim that modern Wi-Fi is actually fast enough for most homes, so worrying about cable faults is unnecessary stress.

stories.headline: How to Maintain Online Anonymity Without Going Off the Grid
stories.summary: PCMag provides comprehensive advice on masking online identity and shielding personal data from surveillance, offering practical steps to remain anonymous while still utilizing internet services effectively.
stories.original_title: Are You as Invisible Online as You Think? Not Unless You're Following Our Advice
stories.why_it_matters: Privacy is becoming harder to keep online, so learning simple tricks protects personal data. This empowers regular people to avoid unwanted tracking.
stories.other_side: Privacy advocates warn that no method is perfect, and determined trackers can still find ways to identify users despite these steps.

stories.headline: Adobe Photoshop 2027 Pre-Cracked Version Circulates Online
stories.summary: A pre-cracked version of Adobe Photoshop 2027 v28.0 has been distributed online, allowing users to access advanced design features such as AI-powered reality reimaging without legitimate licensing.
stories.why_it_matters: Sharing hacked software undermines the hard work of creators and developers. It also exposes users to viruses hidden inside illegal downloads.
stories.other_side: Some users feel that high software prices are unfair and believe they should have access to powerful tools without paying full cost.
